children: The Reserve Bank of India likely intervened in the foreign exchange market on Thursday, four traders told Reuters, as the currency fell past the 96 per dollar mark for the first time in over a month after the U.S. Federal Reserve hiked rates.
was at 96.08 per dollar, down 0.1% from its closing level in the previous session.

State-run banks were spotted offering dollars, most likely on behalf of the RBI, traders said. Persistent central bank intervention has supported the rupee in the face of multiple headwinds ranging from higher oil prices to elevated global bond yields.
